name: check_diagram_placement
title: Check a diagram's print size
description: Calculate print consequences without editing. Supply kind, the exact returned envelope, and positive widthMm and/or heightMm. One dimension derives the other; two define a box and report a proportional fit. Warnings describe reduction or stretching; no universal minimum or booklet fit is assumed. effectivePngDpi concerns PNG only. Venn outputView:pupil|answer selects artwork while retaining pupil source. No baseHash is needed. Use when considering a resize, not at every native-size placement.

name: create_booklet
title: Make an A4 booklet
description: PRODUCE an A4 portrait unit booklet (one lesson per objective) in the MathsDock house style from FINALISED lessons. Supply booklet:{tool:'resource',schemaVersion:1,document:{kind:'booklet-a4',title,code,group?,coverNote?,nameLine?,intro:{remember[],learn[],next[],keywords:[{word,meaning}]}|null,lessons:[1-12 lessons, each {title,code,objective,keyIdea,teacherNotes?,sections:[{kind,title?,instruction?,columns:1|2,cards:[{title,items}]}]}]}}. Section kinds: check-in, worked, practice, diagnostic, mistake, challenge, discover, notes; an empty title uses the kind's heading (Check in, Worked example, Your turn, Diagnostic questions, Spot the mistake, Challenge, Discover, Notes). A booklet is used with the teaching (a worksheet follows it), so each lesson holds the modelling as well as the practice. Recommended lesson shape: a one-sentence key idea naming the new words; check in first (4-5 retrieval questions on this lesson's prerequisites); worked example with columns:2 as pairs, left the worked example with numbered steps and saved answers, right 'Our turn' with the same step labels and the work left blank; Your turn (near-identical questions with the same pre-drawn diagram or empty table, help fading); diagnostic multiple choice with choice mode letters (A-D, each wrong option one named misconception, instruction 'Answer on your mini whiteboard.'); practice that fades with at least three unaided questions per case; spot the mistake with one explain-or-correct card per misconception; a short 'From earlier' check-in strip on earlier work; a challenge; and last 'Exam-style questions' in Edexcel wording with marks as text, e.g. '(Total for Question 2 is 3 marks)'. Name and use the school's method the same way wherever the skill returns, add one new step at a time, and give room for every table or working asked for. Cards use the same items as create_worksheet (text, info, claim, bullets, table, choice, steps, checklist, answerLine, space, diagram, part); worked and notes cards are not numbered, other cards are numbered within their section. Half-width cards (columns:2) are 90.5 mm wide, so a diagram there must fit about 84 mm. Saved answers print only in the answers files; never invent answers the teacher did not give. For a ratio or x → / y ↑ movement table (scaling, gradients, rates) use a ratio-table diagram rather than a plain table, so the curved scaling arrows show the method, in its compact form: {type:'diagram',diagram:{tool:'ratio-table',spec:{columns:['x →','y ↑'],table:[['2','4'],['1','[2]']],steps:['÷ 2']}}}. Cells: '4' printed, '' blank, '_' answer line, '[2]' hidden answer (answers PDF only); headings end in → ↑ or ↓ (y ↓ for negative gradients); steps '× 3' or '÷ 2', '[÷ 2]' hidden for pupils. A whole unit (up to 12 lessons) goes in one call; requests may be up to 512 KiB, so send diagrams as specs rather than full envelopes. Returns previews of the cover and first lesson pages, whole-booklet pupil and answers PDF, pupil and answers Word file (.docx, A4, laid out page for page like the PDFs, fonts embedded) and editable JSON links (kept for 7 days), a pupil and answers PDF and Word link for every lesson, contentHash and layout issues. When issues are returned no files are made: report them and revise. To change a booklet, edit the returned booklet and call create_booklet again.

name: create_worksheet
title: Make an A3 worksheet
description: PRODUCE a two-sided A3 landscape worksheet in the MathsDock house style from a FINALISED question set. Supply resource:{tool:'resource',schemaVersion:1,document:{kind:'worksheet-a3',title,code,objective,group?,nameLine?,notation:'maths' (always on a new worksheet, so {3/4} prints as a stacked fraction),spareSpace:'share' (always on a new worksheet; leave a returned or saved sheet's value as it is),sides:[2 sides, each {instruction?,layout?,score?,columns:[1-3 columns to match layout, each {heading,cards:[{title,stage?,items,working?}]}]}]}}. Cards are numbered automatically across both sides. Items: text, info (pale key-fact card), claim (a pupil's statement), bullets, table (cells with state supplied|blank|hidden), choice (circle|tick|letters options), steps (worked method lines), checklist (pupil tick boxes), answerLine {prefix,suffix,answer,inline}, space {kind:working|drawing,heightMm}, paper {style:squared|dotted|graph,widthMm,heightMm,axes?:{originMm:{x,y}}} (blank grid, optional unnumbered axes), diagram {diagram:{tool:<diagram kind>, envelope}} using the exact envelope a create_diagram call returned, or {tool, spec} with that family's create_diagram spec, and part {text,items} for lettered parts. Text markup is only **bold** and *italic*, plus {3/4} for a stacked fraction: write every fraction this way, never 1/2 or ½. Saved answers (answerLine.answer, hidden cells, hidden diagram values) print only in the answers files (PDF and Word); never invent answers the teacher did not give. Returns side previews, pupil and answers vector PDFs, pupil and answers Word files (.docx, A3, fonts embedded, same layout as the PDFs; editing the pupil .docx does not change the answers .docx or the JSON), editable JSON, contentHash, layout issues and notes. Give the teacher the returned PDF and Word links as links; do not try to download them yourself. A note names a column more than a third blank: the sheet is print-ready, but offer the teacher an extra question there and add it only if they agree. A note naming a question means a fraction there will not print stacked: rewrite it as {3/4} and create again. When issues are returned the sheet is not print-ready: report them and revise the document; do not claim it fits. To change a worksheet, edit the returned resource and call create_worksheet again.

description: Optionally download one existing diagram as ZIP containing editable JSON, outlined SVG, verified 600 ppi PNG, print facts and README. Supply kind and its returned envelope; no baseHash. Does not edit, save a library, or store a booklet. Links expire after seven days; repeat with saved source to refresh. The linked archive is generated on download, so verify retrieval before claiming success. Oversized links may use bounded inline ZIP; otherwise use individual files. name: get_diagram_svg
title: Get a diagram's SVG
description: Retrieve original outlined SVG content through MCP when external SVG downloads are blocked. Supply kind graph/ratio-table/value-graph/cuboids/number-line/venn/algebra-grid/bar-model/charts/probability-tree/frequency-tree/triangle and the exact returned envelope; no URL or baseHash. Venn, charts, probability-tree and frequency-tree outputView defaults pupil; answer must be explicitly requested. Does not revise or save a file. First call: omit offsetBytes; maxChunkBytes defaults to 49152 (1024..49152). Save decoded svgChunk as exact UTF-8 with no extra newline. For continuation use returned nextOffsetBytes and expectedSvgSha256:svgSha256, repeating source/outputView. Verify contiguous offsets, chunkBytes/chunkSha256, unchanged file metadata, then totalBytes/svgSha256 before embedding. sourceContentHash is the revision hash; svgSha256 is a different file checksum. complete means this is the last chunk, not that a client saved a file or printed a PDF. Do not redraw, normalize text, or substitute the preview. If exact saving fails, report the client limitation. Existing download links remain available.
